overview.headline: How the United States elects a president from candidacy to inauguration

keyPoints.point: Election for president happens every four years in November
keyPoints.quote: An election for president of the United States happens every four years on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November.

keyPoints.point: Process of electing a president takes almost two years
keyPoints.quote: The process of electing a president takes almost two years.

keyPoints.point: States and parties hold presidential primaries and caucuses
keyPoints.quote: States and parties hold presidential primaries and caucuses.

keyPoints.point: Electors cast votes for president in Electoral College
keyPoints.quote: Electors cast their votes for president in the Electoral College.

keyPoints.point: Congress counts electoral votes before Inauguration Day

keyTerms.gloss: Commission where Candidates register to run for president
keyTerms.quote: Candidates register with the Federal Election Commission to run for president.

keyTerms.gloss: States and parties hold contests for presidential choice
keyTerms.quote: States and parties hold presidential primaries and caucuses.

keyTerms.gloss: Group where Electors cast votes for president
keyTerms.quote: Electors cast their votes for president in the Electoral College.

keyTerms.gloss: Person that presidential candidate announces during convention
keyTerms.quote: Just before or during the convention, the presidential candidate announces their vice presidential running mate.
